name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.38.1 (released 2026-11-16, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.38.1) is a critical security release that hardens message templating against denial-of-service attacks, fixes S3 attachment memory leaks, and tightens web push subscription limits per IP prefix — upgrading is strongly recommended. v2.38.0 (2026-11-14) introduced cluster-wide rate limit sharing across nodes and patched a DoS bug where crafted templates could build multi-gigabyte strings. v2.37.0 (2026-11-02) added cross-server UnifiedPush subscriber billing via the database, Retry-After and RateLimit headers on HTTP 429 responses, and a 410 Gone response for stale UnifiedPush subscriptions older than 4 days.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL v2 (client apps); check repository for exact details
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in November 2026 with active bug fixes and security patches
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — user database, tier-based access control, and visitor rate limiting with subscriber-based billing
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: With visitor-subscriber-rate-limiting, a UnifiedPush push to a topic with no subscriber for 4 days now returns 410 Gone (error 41002) instead of 507, causing app servers like Mastodon to remove the expired subscription.
Message templating: html, js, and urlquery functions are no longer allowed; printf only accepts plain directives (no explicit argument indexes or %p) and no lists or dicts as arguments.
Message templating: regexMatch, regexFind, and related regex functions now reject patterns longer than 1024 bytes or compiling to more than 5000 instructions.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful multi-platform notification library supporting dozens of services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications and file sharing but is a proprietary cloud service with a limited free tier and no self-hosting capability.

alternatives.name: ntopng Notifications / Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager is a powerful self-hosted alert routing system that integrates deeply with Prometheus but is significantly more complex to set up compared to ntfy's simple HTTP pub-sub model.
